name: Nearby Wi-Fi networks scan
plain: Android lists nearby access points with location permission and throttling; iOS has no public scan.
meaning: The list of nearby BSSIDs locates a phone within meters indoors and enables positioning, which is why scans are location-gated and throttled.

android.note: Foreground 4 scans per 2 minutes, background 1 per 30 minutes (Android 9); can be turned off in Developer options

ios.api_surface: Only for approved captive-portal or Wi-Fi provider apps; no general scan

limits.headline: Can list nearby Wi-Fi networks on Android, with limits and a location prompt
limits.user_action: You tap Allow for Location or Nearby devices when the app asks to scan Wi-Fi
can: List nearby Wi-Fi access points on Android
See names, signal and security type
Scan about 4 times per 2 minutes in the foreground
Use it to guess your indoor spot
cannot: Scan more than about once per 30 minutes in the background on Android 9 and newer
Scan on iPhone unless it is an approved captive portal or Wi-Fi provider
Scan without Location or Nearby devices permission
Skip the scan limits, unless you turn them off in Developer options
limits.differs: Android can scan with location or Nearby devices permission, throttled. iPhone has no public scan.

story.what_it_is: An app can list the Wi-Fi networks around you, which can show where you are.

marketing.name: Wi-Fi scanning
marketing.pitch: Android has Wi-Fi scanning rules that limit how often apps can scan and need location permission.

story.for_you: You do not see the scan. If an app has location permission, it can list nearby routers. That list can tell where you are within a few meters, even inside a building.
story.for_makers: Makers use it for indoor maps, Wi-Fi tools and faster location fixes. The list works like a map key, since every router has a known place. That is why Android limits it and needs location permission.

use_cases.example: A map app improves your blue dot indoors by looking at nearby Wi-Fi.
A Wi-Fi analyzer app shows which channels are crowded so you can fix your router.
A mall app guides you to a store using Wi-Fi positioning inside the building.
A location game checks nearby networks to catch cheaters who fake GPS.
A data company reads the list of routers around you to learn the places you visit.
A security app lists nearby networks to spot a fake copy of a known hotspot.

risks: Tracks you to a few meters
story.android_note: Android lists nearby access points with location permission and limits how often an app can scan.
story.ios_note: iPhone has no public Wi-Fi scan for normal apps.

technical_bounds: Can be limited by Wi-Fi scanning setting
